title: finding(scripts): a changeset that declares a package in its front matter while its body says that package is untouched is mechanically detectable, and no gate reads a changeset against itself
body:
A `.changeset/*.md` that **declares a package in its front matter** while its **body says that package is untouched** is an internal contradiction, it publishes verbatim into the CHANGELOG, and nothing detects it. Caught by hand on PR objectui#9796 this shift; filing the mechanism rather than the instance.

## The instance, verbatim

`.changeset/9710-overlay-trigger-bare-string.md` carried, at head `21896172a9`:

- front matter: `'@object-ui/types': patch`
- body, sixth paragraph: «⛔ **No published face moves.** `packages/types` is **untouched**: the accept set is the one both faces already shipped …»
- body, last paragraph: «**`@object-ui/types` ships corrected read-site documentation, and nothing else.**»
- and the diff moved **62 lines** in `packages/types/src/overlay.ts`.

⇒ the same file declared a patch release for a package, said that package was untouched, and said it shipped corrected documentation. The reader it misleads most is the one diffing their own `.d.ts` after the bump.

⚠️ The sentence was **not** born false — it was true when written in round 1, and this branch's own later CI-fix round falsified it. That is the `BORN FALSE` versus `WENT FALSE` split `scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs`'s own docblock already names.

## Why the five existing gates all miss it, quoting the gate's own header

`scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs:15-22`, verbatim:

> Four gates read `.changeset/` — presence, no-major, fixed, overwrite — and all four judge STRUCTURE: that a declaration exists, what level it declares, how the workspace classifies it, whether a change touched one it does not own. **None of them reads a claim in a body.**

And `check:changeset-claims` itself judges the **cross-file** relation — a pending body that NAMES a file the current change touches. It says so in its own words: it 「judges name resolution, never meaning」, and 「"Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer」.

⇒ nobody reads one changeset against **itself**.

## ⭐ Why this sub-shape is mechanically detectable, and stays inside the gate's own philosophy

This is **not** a request to make a gate understand meaning. It is name resolution between two parts of the SAME file:

1. read the package names in the front matter (already parsed — the presence/no-major/fixed gates all do it);
2. scan the body for a sentence that names one of those packages **adjacent to a negation of change** — `untouched`, `not touched`, `no change`, `unchanged`, `nothing moves`, and the obvious variants;
3. report the pair.

⚠️ A body may legitimately say «no published FACE moves» about a package it patches — which is exactly how PR objectui#9796's changeset was **repaired**, to «No published FACE moves — and one published FILE does». So the check is a **report**, not a refusal, and it belongs in the same report-only, exit-0 posture this gate already has. ⛔ No new blocking gate is proposed, and ⛔ nothing here asks for a prose judgement.

## What would falsify this card

If a scan of the existing `.changeset/` corpus plus recently released CHANGELOG entries finds that this pairing is **always** legitimate phrasing (a face/file distinction like the repair above) and never a live contradiction, the signal is noise and the card should close. ⛔ That scan was **not** run by the filer — it is the first task for whoever takes this, and it decides whether the check is worth its false-positive budget.

## Dedupe words

- changeset front matter declares package body says untouched
- changeset internal contradiction
- one claim two paragraphs
- `check:changeset-claims` reads name resolution only
- changeset prose no gate evaluates
